issues.description: The problem statement and UML consistently refer to a class named "Stock" (and specify a SealSaloon field of type Stock), but the template and solution repositories provide/use a class named Inventory (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Inventory.java) while src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java is empty in the template. This naming mismatch (Stock vs Inventory) is likely to confuse students and may cause compilation or implementation errors if they follow the problem text literally.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class name consistent across all artifacts. Options: (a) Update the problem statement and UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock (and remove or repurpose the empty Stock.java), or (b) rename Inventory.java to Stock.java (and update usages in the solution and template accordingly) and provide a proper implementation in Stock.java. Ensure the SealSaloon specification (type of the shared stock attribute and related method signatures) matches the actual class provided in the template.
